page: Microsoft Azure E20_v4 is a memory-optimized virtual machine instance belonging to the Ev4 server family. Running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 20 dedicated vCPUs mapped from 10 physical Intel Xeon 8272CL cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a base clock speed of 2.6 GHz and includes 35 MB of L3 cache. It is equipped with 160.0 GB of system memory, yielding a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 8.0 GB per vCPU. The instance does not include local storage or integrated GPUs, requiring external network-attached storage for persistent data.

Benchmark data indicates balanced performance across most workloads, with a strong Passmark memory score placing it in the top tier of memory performance. Memory bandwidth tests show read-only speeds of 1034.46 GB/sec for cached small blocks and 88.48 GB/sec for uncached large blocks, alongside a write speed of 43.27 GB/sec. Single-core and multi-core CPU performance metrics, such as stress-ng and Geekbench scores, fall consistently within the average range. However, single-threaded bzip3 decompression is relatively weak at 8.63 GB/sec, and prompt processing for medium 7B LLM models is limited to 29.26 tokens/sec, highlighting a performance tradeoff in single-threaded decompression and complex local inference tasks.

From a cost-efficiency perspective, the E20_v4 offers a high-density memory profile relative to its compute resources, making it a viable option for memory-intensive workloads that do not require local NVMe storage or GPU acceleration. The instance is well-suited for relational databases, in-memory caching layers like Redis, enterprise applications, and data processing tasks. The high memory capacity supports larger working datasets, while the dedicated Intel Xeon vCPUs provide stable execution for multi-threaded application servers and general-purpose business logic.
description: Microsoft Azure E20_v4 is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine from the Ev4 family, powered by an Intel Xeon 8272CL processor running at 2.6 GHz. It features 20 dedicated vCPUs across 10 physical cores, 160.0 GB of RAM, and no local storage or GPUs. Operating under Microsoft Hyper-V, the instance delivers strong memory performance, as evidenced by its high Passmark memory score and a 1034.46 GB/sec cached read bandwidth. While multi-threaded performance and database operations are average, single-threaded bzip3 decompression and medium-model LLM prompt processing show relative weakness. This instance is qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-heavy applications, making it suitable for in-memory databases, caching layers, and enterprise workloads requiring a high RAM-to-vCPU ratio without local storage needs.
